# EdgeBalancer
> Control plane for deploying Cloudflare Worker load balancers and API gateways without writing Worker code. Bring your Cloudflare account, pick origins and strategy, we deploy the Worker.

## When to use EdgeBalancer
Use EdgeBalancer when you need to deploy or manage Cloudflare Worker-based load balancers or API gateways without writing Worker code yourself. The platform supports 7 load balancing strategies (round-robin, weighted round-robin, IP hash, sticky sessions, weighted sticky sessions, failover, geographic steering) and 9 API gateway features (JWT validation, header transforms, response caching, canary splitting, IP allow/deny, mock routes, rate limiting, path routing, CORS). If you have a Cloudflare account and need traffic routing across multiple origins, EdgeBalancer handles the Worker generation, deployment, versioning, and rollback — you configure via a visual dashboard or the AI agent. Pricing starts at free (5 load balancers, all strategies included).

## When NOT to use EdgeBalancer
Do not use EdgeBalancer if you need DNS-based load balancing (use Cloudflare Load Balancing directly), if you don't have a Cloudflare account, or if you need to manage non-Cloudflare infrastructure. EdgeBalancer is a control plane — it never proxies your traffic. If you need direct Cloudflare API access for non-Worker resources, use the Cloudflare dashboard.

## How EdgeBalancer works for agents
EdgeBalancer is an API-first platform. The AI agent at https://edge.nexoral.in accepts natural language instructions and executes them as API calls. You can:
- Create, update, delete, pause, and resume load balancers via the AI agent
- Create, update, and delete API gateways via the AI agent
- List your load balancers and gateways
- All operations are real — the AI agent calls the same API endpoints as the dashboard
- The AI agent requires a signed-in session (JWT cookie) and a connected Cloudflare account
- Destructive actions (update, delete, pause, resume) require in-conversation confirmation before execution
- The AI agent uses a model ladder: OpenRouter free tier → Mistral metered tier
- Rate limit: 3 AI runs per 15 minutes per user

## API endpoints
All endpoints are under https://edge.nexoral.in/api. Authentication is via httpOnly JWT cookies (Firebase Google OAuth → JWT).

### Load Balancers
- GET /api/loadbalancers — list user's load balancers
- POST /api/loadbalancers — create (validates hostname, deploys Worker)
- GET /api/loadbalancers/:id — get single load balancer
- PUT /api/loadbalancers/:id — update (uses CF Worker Versions, rollback on failure)
- DELETE /api/loadbalancers/:id — delete (removes Worker + domain)
- POST /api/loadbalancers/validate-hostname — preflight hostname conflict check
- POST /api/loadbalancers/operations/:operationId/cancel — cancel in-flight create/update
- POST /api/loadbalancers/:id/pause — pause (release-domain or keep-domain)
- POST /api/loadbalancers/:id/resume — resume paused load balancer

### API Gateways
- GET /api/gateways — list user's gateways
- POST /api/gateways — create gateway
- GET /api/gateways/:id — get single gateway
- PUT /api/gateways/:id — update gateway
- DELETE /api/gateways/:id — delete gateway
- POST /api/gateways/:id/pause — pause gateway
- POST /api/gateways/:id/resume — resume paused gateway

### Sessions (deployment history)
- GET /api/sessions — cursor-paginated list (filter: all/active/inactive)
- GET /api/sessions/:id/script — raw Worker JS for a session

### AI Agent
- POST /api/ai/generate — { prompt, messages? } → SSE stream of the agent turn. 3 per 15 min.
- GET /api/ai/runs — cursor-paginated run history
- GET /api/ai/runs/:id — single run with full steps

### Auth
- POST /api/auth/google — Firebase ID token → JWT
- POST /api/auth/logout — clears session + challenge cookies
- GET /api/auth/me — current user (protected)

### Cloudflare
- POST /api/cloudflare/credentials — save CF account ID + API token
- PUT /api/cloudflare/credentials — update CF credentials
- GET /api/cloudflare/credentials — get masked credentials
- GET /api/cloudflare/zones — list CF zones from user account

## How it works
Internet → Cloudflare (330+ PoPs) → Worker (your account) → Origins. Control plane never touches data.

## FAQ

### How is this different from Cloudflare Load Balancing?
Cloudflare Load Balancing is a DNS-based solution ($5/balancer + per-query fees). EdgeBalancer deploys as a Worker script, giving you request-level control with no per-query costs. You pay only for Worker requests (100k/day free, then $0.30/M).

### Can I bring my own domains?
Yes. You connect your Cloudflare account, and we deploy Workers to zones you already own. You maintain full control — delete the API token and the Workers stay deployed under your account.

### What happens if EdgeBalancer goes down?
Your load balancers keep running. Once deployed, the Worker script lives in your Cloudflare account. EdgeBalancer is only the control plane for creating and updating configs — the data plane runs independently on Cloudflare's edge.

### How do updates work?
Updates use Cloudflare Worker Versions and Deployments. When you change a config, we create a new version, deploy it, and keep the previous version as a rollback target. Old inactive versions are pruned automatically.

### Can I see the generated Worker code?
Yes. All Worker scripts are visible in your Cloudflare dashboard under Workers & Pages. The code is generated from strategy-specific templates.

### What are the performance implications?
Workers add ~1-3ms median overhead. The benefit is intelligent routing, health checks, and failover at the edge — much faster than round-tripping to a centralized load balancer.

### Do you store or proxy my traffic?
No. EdgeBalancer never sees your production traffic. We store only metadata (origin URLs, weights, strategy choice) encrypted in MongoDB. All requests flow directly from Cloudflare edge to your origins.

### How do I delete everything?
Delete load balancers from the dashboard, then rotate your API token. You can also manually delete the Worker scripts from Cloudflare's dashboard. EdgeBalancer has no lock-in — everything runs in your account.
